rows:
The teacher greets his learners / the learners respond.
A short review about must and mustn’t.
The teacher asks his learners to give examples and in which case they use must.
To reinforce and to pave the way at the same time

The teacher invites his learners to compare the 4 sentences:
> a) You **must** do more exercise to keep fit.
> b) You **have to** take with you the doctor’s prescription.
> c) You **mustn’t** forget your prescription if you want to buy medicine.
> d) If you don’t like cheese, you **don’t have to** eat it.

- Discuss the differences between ‘have to’ and ‘must’ in the positive form.
Why do we have to take the prescription with us? Because the chemist will ask for it.
So sentence b has a sense of an **external obligation**.
- Discuss the differences between ‘don’t have to’ and ‘mustn’t’. Make sure to stress the idea that ‘don’t have to’ expresses the idea that the person isn’t required to do something but may do so if he/she would like, while ‘mustn’t’ expresses the idea of prohibition.

The teacher highlights the rules:
! To talk about something that is **necessary** for me or another person to do (because it’s **a law**, **a duty** or **a fact**) we use: “**Have / has to + stem**”
! Eg: We **have to** get a passport if we want to travel to another country. (**a law**)
! She **has to** take care of her sick mother. (**a duty**)
! I **have to** go now because I have an appointment with my dietitian. (**a fact**)

## Past simple
Auxiliary: DO – **DID** – DONE
**Regular verbs (-ed)**
| |Base form|Past form| |
|---|---|---|---|
|to|play|play**ed**|play**ed**|
|to|walk|walk**ed**|walk**ed**|
|to|study|stud**ied**|stud**ied**|
**Affirmative:** subject + base form + -ed
Ex. I / you / he / she / it / we / they **played** football yesterday.

**Irregular verbs (different ways)**
| |Base form|Past form| |
|---|---|---|---|
|to|make|made|made|
|to|ring|rang|rung|
|to|go|went|gone|
**Affirmative:** subject + 2nd form
Ex. I / you / he / she / it / we / they **went** to the cinema.

**Negative:** subject + DIDN’T + base form
|Regular verbs:|Ex. I / you / he / she / it / we / they **didn’t play** football yesterday.|
|Irregular verbs:|Ex. I / you / he / she / it / we / they **didn’t go** to the cinema last night.|

**Interrogative (Yes / No quest.):** DID + subject + base form ?
|Regular verbs:|Ex. **Did** I / you / he / she / it / we / they **play** football yesterday?|
|Irregular verbs:|Ex. **Did** I / you / he / she / it / we / they **go** to the cinema last night?|

**Interrogative (Wh- quest.):** Wh- word + DID + subject + base form ?
|Regular verbs:|Ex. **What did** I / you / he / she / it / we / they **play** yesterday? **Football**|
|Irregular verbs:|Ex. **Where did** I / you / he / she / it / we / they **go** last night? **To the cinema**|
